newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Ascom shuffles Timeplex, partner sought.
newsitem.headline: Ascom shuffles Timeplex, partner sought.

text.p: Swiss telecommunications group Ascom Holding AG said it had cut 270 jobs as part of a sweeping restructuring of its Ascom Timeplex Inc. unit as it continues the search for a cooperation partner.

Chief financial officer Jakob Schlapbach told reporters that negotiations with a partner for Timeplex collapsed during the summer, when the potential partner encountered profitability problems and withdrew from the talks.
Chairman Felix Wittlin said the level of 1996 net profit would depend on possible provisions and restructuring costs in connection with the search for a partner for troubled Ascom unit Timeplex.
"The group net profit will strongly depend on the search for a partner (for Timeplex)," Wittlin told reporters during a news conference to present half-year results.
But Ascom expected its operating profit in 1996 to exceed last year's result, assuming that markets remain stable, a company statement said.

Ascom said group operating profit for the first half of 1996 was 39 million Swiss francs ($31.5 million) versus 28 million a year earlier. First half revenue rose to 1.403 billion as against 1.398 billion Swiss francs.

On the search for a Timeplex partner, Schlapbach said talks were underway with new candidates and Ascom was still open to a wide range of possibilities, including an outright sale of Timeplex or a majority or minority stake by another company.
Timeplex has long been a problem child for Ascom, which bought the New Jersey-based company in 1991.
Timeplex, a leader in the area of enterprise networks, forms the core of Ascom's Enterprise Network segment, which recorded a loss of 39 million Swiss francs in the first half of 1996.
In addition to cutting 270 jobs, or about one-fifth of Timeplex personnel, a new management team has been installed and Timeplex has focused its product strategy on Wide Area Networks (WAN).
Job cuts were completed by the end of September and Ascom took restructuring costs and provisions in the first half, pushing extraordinary items into a loss of 15 million francs.
Timeplex is currently trying to make up for a delayed launch of its Synchrony range of products, which has won positive feedback from customers and an increasing order book.
However, Ascom admits that it lost customers due to the delayed launch and it is an uphill battle to win them back. ($ = 1.24 Swiss Francs)
